intelligence.human_view: Think of it like handing someone a menu of dishes that aren't on the table yet. The dishes exist — they're cooked, they're in the kitchen, verified — but he can't see them, can't taste them, can't open them. He asked for the meal, not the menu. The report is only a report when the notes are on the table — live on the Hub feed, where his eye can open each one. Until then, hold it.
intelligence.simple_view: A list of note names you can't open is not a report! The notes have to be LIVE on the Hub — where you can see them and open them — before the report goes out! Filed is not live!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — a list of names you can't open is not a report, dear! The notes have to be right there on the Hub, love, where you can see them and open them, before the report goes out! Filed is not live, dear!
intelligence.naya_view: Hold the delivery until the notes are live. A report is a list of things he can open — on the Hub feed, rendered, proven by a real render — not a list of names filed on GitHub. Filed ≠ live, and a filed-but-not-live list is noise. The fix round proves all 40 render live on the Hub before the report is sent; if the pipeline cannot carry a note, name it and say what needs his hand — never a manual production write from this seat. And keep the series straight: the weekly series is the week's lessons distilled, not the welcome mail series — two different things, never confused.
